Card Duel Rules

Two mages duel with creatures and spells. Whoever brings the other mage from 20 life down to 0 wins.

The rules

Decks
Each player plays one of four ready-made decks of 30 cards (ten different cards, three of each): Forest has many small creatures that grow back, Fire deals damage directly, Water draws cards and sends creatures back, Stone has few but strong defenders. Both players may choose the same deck.
Power
In your first turn you have 1 power, then 1 more each turn, at most 10. Every card costs power (the number in the circle); power you don't use is lost at the end of the turn.
A turn
Draw a card, play cards, attack with your creatures, then End turn. At most 6 creatures per side and 10 cards in hand; a card drawn into a full hand is lost. With an empty deck, drawing costs your mage 2 life instead.
Creatures and spells
A creature stays on the table with attack and life (3 / 5 means attack 3, life 5). A spell works once and is then gone. Damage on a creature stays until it is defeated at 0 life.
Attacking
A creature attacks from the turn after it was played, once per turn. You choose the target: the other mage or one of their creatures. Two creatures hit each other at the same time with their attack.
Who starts
Chosen at random. To even it out, the other player starts with 4 cards instead of 3 and has 1 power more in their first turn, and the very first turn of the game draws no card.
Abilities
Some cards have one of six abilities; tapping a card or creature during the game explains them:
Bulwark
Must be attacked first: while it stands, the other side can attack neither the mage nor another creature.
Nimble
Can attack in the same turn it is played.
Thick Skin
Takes 1 damage less from every hit.
Regrow
Gets 2 life back at the end of your turn (up to its full life).
Insight
When it is played, you draw a card.
Ember
When it is played, the other mage takes 2 damage.
Playing
Tap a card in your hand, then Play; a spell that needs a target asks for one. To attack, tap one of your ready creatures (thick frame), then a target with a dashed frame. The list below shows the last moves, including the computer's. Against the computer: Easy often plays at random, Medium takes the move that looks best right now, Hard also weighs the other side's answer. On one device the hand is covered between turns.

Example

Your Ash Wolf (3 / 3) attacks the Mist Otter (2 / 4, Bulwark). The otter takes 3 damage and keeps 1 life, the wolf takes 2 and keeps 1. As long as the otter stands, the other mage cannot be attacked.
